claims.source_quote_ar: يُقْرَأُ عَلَى مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ
claims.claim_ar: وَوُفِّيَتْ: فعل ماضٍ مبني للمجهول؛ و«كُلُّ نَفْسٍ» نائبُ الفاعل مرفوعٌ (كُلُّ مرفوعة)، لأن الفعل مبني للمجهول والقائم مقام الفاعل ظاهر بعده.
claims.claim_en: The verb وُفِّيَتْ is a past passive (built for the passive); "كُلُّ نَفْسٍ" functions as the na'ib al-fa'il (subject substitute) in the nominative, since the verb is passive and the entity standing for the agent follows it.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source chunk states the general rule about verbs read/used when their agent is not named (يُقْرَأُ عَلَى مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ) but does not analyze this specific verse; the assignment of نائب الفاعل to "كُلُّ نَفْسٍ" is an application of that general rule and should be reviewed against the full commentary for this ayah.
